password.title: Password
password.definition: A secret used to authenticate an account.

password-manager.title: Password manager
password-manager.definition: A tool that stores unique passwords securely.

phishing.title: Phishing
phishing.definition: A deceptive message that tries to steal information or money.

otp.title: One-time password
otp.definition: A short-lived code that must never be shared.

domain.title: Domain
domain.definition: The registered name that identifies a website.

wpa3.title: WPA3
wpa3.definition: A modern standard for protecting Wi-Fi networks.

permission.title: App permission
permission.definition: A rule that controls which device resources an app can access.

firewall.title: Firewall
firewall.definition: A control that permits or blocks network connections.

parameterized-query.title: Parameterized query
parameterized-query.definition: A database query that keeps input separate from instructions.

incident-response.title: Incident response
incident-response.definition: A planned process to contain, investigate and recover from an incident.

passkey.title: Passkey
passkey.definition: A sign-in credential tied to a device or account that resists common password phishing.

sim-swap.title: SIM swap
sim-swap.definition: An attempt to move a phone number to a different SIM without the owner's permission.

vpn.title: Virtual private network
vpn.definition: A protected tunnel to a trusted network service; it does not make every website trustworthy.

qr-payment.title: QR payment scam
qr-payment.definition: A payment trick that uses a QR code to send a victim to an unsafe action or page.

ransomware.title: Ransomware
ransomware.definition: Malware that can block access to files and demand payment.

isolation.title: Isolation
isolation.definition: Separating a suspected device or account to limit further impact.

backup.title: Backup
backup.definition: A separate copy of information that can be used to recover it.

privacy-controls.title: Privacy controls
privacy-controls.definition: Settings that limit who can see personal information.

recovery-method.title: Recovery method
recovery-method.definition: A verified alternate way to regain access to an account.

authentication-log.title: Authentication log
authentication-log.definition: A record of sign-in events and their outcomes.

rate-limit.title: Rate limit
rate-limit.definition: A control that limits how often an action can be repeated.

mfa.title: Multi-factor authentication
mfa.definition: Sign-in protection that requires more than one type of proof.

file-permissions.title: File permissions
file-permissions.definition: Rules that define who can read, change or run a file.

least-privilege.title: Least privilege
least-privilege.definition: Giving an account only the access needed for its task.

ownership.title: File ownership
ownership.definition: The user or group that controls a file or resource.

spf.title: SPF
spf.definition: An email-domain policy that lists permitted sending systems.

dkim.title: DKIM
dkim.definition: A signature that helps verify an email was authorized by its sending domain.

dmarc.title: DMARC
dmarc.definition: A policy that uses SPF and DKIM alignment to guide email handling.

hashing.title: Hashing
hashing.definition: A one-way transformation used to verify data without storing its original value.

salting.title: Salting
salting.definition: Adding a unique random value before hashing to protect stored password hashes.

encryption.title: Encryption
encryption.definition: Transforming data so it can be read only with the appropriate key.

sql-injection.title: SQL injection
sql-injection.definition: A risk caused when untrusted input is treated as part of a database command.

input-validation.title: Input validation
input-validation.definition: Checking that data matches expected types and limits before use.

xss.title: Cross-site scripting
xss.definition: A risk where untrusted web content is interpreted as active page content.

output-encoding.title: Output encoding
output-encoding.definition: Converting characters so untrusted text displays as data, not markup.

csp.title: Content security policy
csp.definition: A browser policy that restricts which sources may provide page content.

secret.title: Secret
secret.definition: A private key, token or credential that must not be exposed.

secret-scanning.title: Secret scanning
secret-scanning.definition: Automated checks that look for credentials accidentally added to code.

gitignore.title: .gitignore
gitignore.definition: A project file that tells Git which local files not to include in new commits.

broken-access-control.title: Broken access control
broken-access-control.definition: A flaw where a user can access data or actions beyond their authorization.

authorization.title: Authorization
authorization.definition: A check that decides what an identified user is allowed to access.

cloud-bucket.title: Cloud storage bucket
cloud-bucket.definition: A cloud storage container whose access should be explicitly controlled.

iam-role.title: Identity and access role
iam-role.definition: A cloud identity role that grants a defined set of permissions.

sandbox.title: Sandbox
sandbox.definition: An isolated environment used to observe a file without using real systems.

malware.title: Malware
malware.definition: Software designed to perform unwanted or harmful actions.

forensic-timeline.title: Forensic timeline
forensic-timeline.definition: An ordered account of evidence and events during an investigation.

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.definition: Information preserved to help understand and review an incident.

insider-threat.title: Insider threat
insider-threat.definition: A risk involving misuse of legitimate access by someone inside an organization.

data-loss-prevention.title: Data loss prevention
data-loss-prevention.definition: Controls that help prevent sensitive information leaving approved locations.

attack-chain.title: Attack chain
attack-chain.definition: A sequence of actions an attacker may take to reach a goal.

containment.title: Containment
containment.definition: Actions that limit an incident's further spread or impact.

triage.title: Alert triage
triage.definition: Sorting alerts by urgency, evidence and potential impact.

eradication.title: Eradication
eradication.definition: Removing the cause of an incident after it has been contained.

recovery.title: Recovery
recovery.definition: Restoring normal service safely after an incident.

3-2-1-backup.title: 3-2-1 backup rule
3-2-1-backup.definition: Keep three copies on two storage types, with one copy off-site.

evil-twin.title: Evil twin network
evil-twin.definition: A fake Wi-Fi access point that imitates a trusted network name.

https.title: HTTPS
https.definition: A web connection protected with TLS; check the domain as well as the lock indicator.

perfect-level.title: Perfect Level
perfect-level.description: Complete a level without mistakes or hints.

code-reviewer.title: Code Reviewer
code-reviewer.description: Complete a secure code review level.

no-hints-chapter.title: Independent Defender
no-hints-chapter.description: Complete a full chapter without hints.

seven-day-streak.title: Seven-Day Streak
seven-day-streak.description: Complete levels on seven consecutive days.
